name: explicit dated observation
messages: My ankle was sore from 2026-10-05 through 2026-10-07.
rubric: Preserves subjective soreness without a diagnosis or running prohibition.

name: reported professional constraint
messages: My physio told me to avoid hills until reassessment. This is a personal restriction I want remembered.
rubric: Attributes guidance to the user's report of a physio.
Preserves the end condition without guessing an end date.

name: hypothetical
messages: If my ankle were sore, would that affect today's training? It isn't sore; this is hypothetical. Don't remember this example.
rubric: Does not capture the hypothetical or invent a constraint.

name: third person
messages: My friend's ankle is sore. I am asking for general information, not describing my own condition.
rubric: Does not turn another person's report into a personal observation.

name: tentative suggestion
messages: Maybe I should avoid hills? This is a question, not a decision or established restriction.
rubric: Discusses uncertainty rather than recording an established constraint.

name: explicit noncapture
messages: I slept poorly last night, but do not remember this.
rubric: Respects the explicit request not to save.

name: two distinct observations
messages: I felt tired on 2026-10-05. I slept poorly on 2026-10-06. Remember both reports.
rubric: Records separate reports with distinct dates and evidence spans.

name: change is not a correction
messages: My ankle felt sore on 2026-10-05.
On 2026-10-07 it felt better. That is a later change, not a correction of the earlier report.
rubric: Keeps both observations without implying that improvement cancels restrictions.

name: correct a date
messages: My ankle was sore on 2026-10-05.
Correction: that soreness was on 2026-10-06, not 2026-10-05. Correct the entry.
rubric: Corrects the existing entry rather than creating a second observation.

name: cross-thread dated context
messages: My coach told me to avoid hills until we review it. Remember that restriction.
follow_up: What should I consider when choosing today's training?
rubric: Takes the restriction into account in a new thread.
Does not claim the coach's advice was independently verified.
Does not invent an additional restriction or diagnosis.

name: goal horizon and no invented target
messages: I want to improve my swimming speed over the next six weeks. Remember that goal; I have no target pace.
rubric: Includes the goal across threads without an invented pace or priority.
Uses 42 inclusive local dates anchored to the source timestamp.
Respects constraints and coach prescriptions; no plan rewrite.

name: goal closure and explicit resumption
messages: I want to build swimming endurance. Remember this open-ended goal.
I withdrew that swimming goal on 2020-01-01; close it as withdrawn.
I explicitly want to resume that same goal now. Clear its closure; do not create a duplicate.
rubric: Keeps the same entry through explicit closure/resumption.
Neither silence nor improved observations imply achievement.

name: classification correction
messages: I can only swim twice a week. Remember this restriction.
Correction: that entry should describe my goal to swim twice a week, not a limitation. Reclassify it as a goal.
rubric: Reads and corrects the same ID without requiring the original report again.
Clears incompatible lifecycle fields and preserves historical discussion.

name: withdrawal with unrelated continuation
messages: I can only swim on Tuesdays. Remember that restriction. Also explain bicycle gearing.
Forget that Tuesday swimming restriction, then continue explaining bicycle gearing.
What was the bicycle gearing comparison?
rubric: Confirms only the committed forget and completes the unrelated comparison.
Does not infer that Tuesday availability was false or that swimming is now unlimited.
Uses the withdrawal notice alongside unchanged history; unlabelled echoes remain a quality concern.

name: overdue goal is not achieved
messages: Remember my goal: improve swimming endurance from 2020-01-01 through 2020-02-11. I have never confirmed completing or withdrawing it.
follow_up: How should we interpret that old goal now?
rubric: Asks whether the overdue goal remains relevant without assuming achievement or renewed commitment.

name: ambiguous indivisible evidence
messages: I need to swim less. This is only a tentative idea, not accepted intent or a confirmed restriction. Discuss it without saving yet.
rubric: Clarifies meaning rather than using a keyword to record multiple kinds from one quote.

name: superseded historical conclusion
messages: Remember: my ankle felt sore on 2020-01-01. Explain how you interpret this old report.
Correction: that report was about 2020-01-02. Update its date.
Compare your earlier interpretation with the corrected report. Do not infer ongoing soreness.
rubric: Explains the historical conclusion using original discussion, then applies the current revision.
Preserves uncertainty and does not infer a present symptom or recovery.

messages: I felt tired on 2020-01-01. I felt tired on 2020-01-02. Remember both dated reports separately.
rubric: Uses full distinct clauses or precise Unicode occurrence offsets for repeated words.
Does not silently switch evidence occurrences after ambiguity or claim general semantic deduplication.
